/-!
# Conjecture 6.29

by O. V. Mel'nikov

Suppose that a finite group $A$ is isomorphic to the group of all topological
automorphisms of a locally compact group $G$. Does there always exist a discrete
group whose automorphism group is isomorphic to $A$? This is true if $A$ is
cyclic; the condition of local compactness of $G$ is essential
(R. J. Wille, *Indag. Math.* **25**, no. 2 (1963), 218–224).

A topological automorphism of a topological group $G$ is a group automorphism
of $G$ that is also a homeomorphism, that is, both it and its inverse are
continuous. Topological groups are assumed to be Hausdorff. The automorphism
group of a discrete group is the automorphism group of its underlying abstract
group, since every map out of a discrete space is continuous.

*References:*
- [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46), Problem 6.29.
- R. J. Wille, *Indag. Math.* **25**, no. 2 (1963), 218–224.
-/

def continuousMulAut (G : Type*) [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G] : Subgroup (MulAut G) where
  carrier := {f | Continuous f ∧ Continuous f.symm}
  one_mem' := ⟨continuous_id, continuous_id⟩
  mul_mem' hf hg := ⟨hf.1.comp hg.1, hg.2.comp hf.2⟩
  inv_mem' hf := ⟨hf.2, hf.1⟩

The group of all topological automorphisms of a topological group `G`: the subgroup of

justification.closest_existing_considered: `ContinuousMulEquiv` (`G ≃ₜ* G`, no group structure in Mathlib), `MulAut G` (all abstract automorphisms, ignores topology), `Homeomorph` (no group structure on self-homeomorphisms in Mathlib either).
justification.name: Kourovka.«6.29».continuousMulAut
justification.why_needed: The problem is about the group of all topological automorphisms of a topological group G (group automorphisms that are homeomorphisms). Mathlib has `ContinuousMulEquiv` (`G ≃ₜ* G`) but provides no `Group` instance on it and no named topological automorphism group, and nothing in FormalConjecturesForMathlib either. `continuousMulAut G : Subgroup (MulAut G)` is the subgroup `{f | Continuous f ∧ Continuous f.symm}`; its coercion to a type carries the induced group structure, so `A ≃* continuousMulAut G` expresses A ≅ TopAut(G). Accompanied by an `@[category API]` membership lemma and an `@[category test]` lemma that it is `⊤` for a discrete topology.

theorem continuousMulAut_eq_top_of_discreteTopology (G : Type*) [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G]

@[category research open, AMS 20 22]
theorem kourovka.«6.29» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (A : Type) [Group A] [Finite A] (G : Type) [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G]
      [IsTopologicalGroup G] [T2Space G] [LocallyCompactSpace G],

      ∃ (H : Type) (_ : Group H), Nonempty (MulAut H ≃* A) := by

/-!
# Conjecture 6.29

by O. V. Mel'nikov

Suppose that a finite group $A$ is isomorphic to the group of all topological
automorphisms of a locally compact group $G$. Does there always exist a discrete
group whose automorphism group is isomorphic to $A$? This is true if $A$ is
cyclic; the condition of local compactness of $G$ is essential
(R. J. Wille, *Indag. Math.* **25**, no. 2 (1963), 218–224).

A topological automorphism of a topological group $G$ is a group automorphism
of $G$ that is also a homeomorphism, that is, both it and its inverse are
continuous. Topological groups are assumed to be Hausdorff. The automorphism
group of a discrete group is the automorphism group of its underlying abstract
group, since every map out of a discrete space is continuous.

*References:*
- [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46), Problem 6.29.
- R. J. Wille, *Indag. Math.* **25**, no. 2 (1963), 218–224.
-/

namespace Kourovka.«6.29»

/-- The group of all topological automorphisms of a topological group `G`: the subgroup of
`MulAut G` consisting of the automorphisms that are homeomorphisms, i.e. both the
automorphism and its inverse are continuous. -/
def continuousMulAut (G : Type*) [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G] : Subgroup (MulAut G) where
  carrier := {f | Continuous f ∧ Continuous f.symm}
  one_mem' := ⟨continuous_id, continuous_id⟩
  mul_mem' hf hg := ⟨hf.1.comp hg.1, hg.2.comp hf.2⟩
  inv_mem' hf := ⟨hf.2, hf.1⟩

@[category API, AMS 20 22]
theorem mem_continuousMulAut {G : Type*} [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G] (f : MulAut G) :
    f ∈ continuousMulAut G ↔ Continuous f ∧ Continuous f.symm :=
  Iff.rfl

/-- For a discrete group, every automorphism is a topological automorphism. This is why the
question below is trivial when $G$ is itself discrete. -/
@[category test, AMS 20 22]
theorem continuousMulAut_eq_top_of_discreteTopology (G : Type*) [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G]
    [DiscreteTopology G] : continuousMulAut G = ⊤ :=
  Subgroup.eq_top_iff' _ |>.mpr fun _ => ⟨continuous_of_discreteTopology,
    continuous_of_discreteTopology⟩

/--
Suppose that a finite group $A$ is isomorphic to the group of all topological
automorphisms of a locally compact group $G$. Does there always exist a discrete
group whose automorphism group is isomorphic to $A$?

Here $G$ is a Hausdorff locally compact topological group, and its group of
topological automorphisms is `continuousMulAut G`. A discrete group is an abstract
group `H`, whose automorphism group is `MulAut H`.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20 22]
theorem kourovka.«6.29» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (A : Type) [Group A] [Finite A] (G : Type) [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G]
      [IsTopologicalGroup G] [T2Space G] [LocallyCompactSpace G],
      Nonempty (A ≃* continuousMulAut G) →
      ∃ (H : Type) (_ : Group H), Nonempty (MulAut H ≃* A) := by
  sorry

/--
If a finite cyclic group $A$ is isomorphic to the group of all topological
automorphisms of a locally compact (Hausdorff) group $G$, then there exists a
discrete group whose automorphism group is isomorphic to $A$
(R. J. Wille, *Indag. Math.* **25**, no. 2 (1963), 218–224).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 20 22]
theorem kourovka.«6.29».variants.cyclic :
    ∀ (A : Type) [Group A] [Finite A] [IsCyclic A] (G : Type) [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G]
      [IsTopologicalGroup G] [T2Space G] [LocallyCompactSpace G],
      Nonempty (A ≃* continuousMulAut G) →
      ∃ (H : Type) (_ : Group H), Nonempty (MulAut H ≃* A) := by
  sorry

/--
The condition of local compactness of $G$ is essential: there is a (Hausdorff)
topological group $G$, not locally compact, whose group of all topological
automorphisms is finite but is not isomorphic to the automorphism group of any
discrete group (R. J. Wille, *Indag. Math.* **25**, no. 2 (1963), 218–224).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 20 22]
theorem kourovka.«6.29».variants.local_compactness_essential :
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G) (_ : TopologicalSpace G),
      IsTopologicalGroup G ∧ T2Space G ∧ ¬ LocallyCompactSpace G ∧
      Finite (continuousMulAut G) ∧
      ∀ (H : Type) [Group H], IsEmpty (MulAut H ≃* continuousMulAut G) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«6.29»

items: Hausdorffness (`T2Space G`) is a standing hypothesis on the topological group G in all three slots, following the usual convention that a 'locally compact group' / 'topological group' in this context is Hausdorff (as the decomposition notes request).

'Topological automorphism' is read as a group automorphism that is a homeomorphism (both it and its inverse continuous), encoded by `continuousMulAut G : Subgroup (MulAut G)`; A ≅ TopAut(G) is `Nonempty (A ≃* continuousMulAut G)` (abstract group isomorphism).

'Discrete group whose automorphism group is isomorphic to A' is encoded as an abstract group `H : Type` with `Nonempty (MulAut H ≃* A)`, since every automorphism of a discrete group is a topological automorphism (recorded by the test lemma `continuousMulAut_eq_top_of_discreteTopology`).

In the local_compactness_essential slot, I did NOT add `¬ LocallyCompactSpace G` as an explicit conjunct: 'the condition is essential' is read as 'the statement fails once the hypothesis is dropped', i.e. exactly the negation of the generalised statement. (Wille's example is in fact non-locally-compact, and adding the conjunct would give an equally true but slightly stronger claim.)
All types are quantified in `Type` (universe 0), following the repository's Kourovka files.

In the essential slot the finite group A is kept as an explicit existentially quantified group (rather than writing `Finite (continuousMulAut G)`), to mirror the main statement; the two are equivalent.

Topological automorphisms are modelled as `G ≃ₜ* G`, i.e. group automorphisms that are homeomorphisms (both directions continuous). This is the standard meaning; for locally compact groups one does not in general get continuity of the inverse for free, so bicontinuity is required explicitly via the bundled type.
Hausdorffness (`T2Space G`) is imposed on every topological group, following the notebook's standing convention, in all three slots.

The bespoke `Group (G ≃ₜ* G)` instance is declared globally (inside the file's namespace but instances are global) with `[Group G] [TopologicalSpace G]`; if Mathlib later adds such an instance this file would need updating. It uses the `MulAut` convention `f * g = g.trans f`.

All types (`A`, `G`, `H`) live in `Type`, following the repository idiom (cf. Kourovka/1_40, 1_74, 19_25). `A` is finite via `[Finite A]`; the isomorphism `A ≅ TopAut(G)` is `Nonempty (A ≃* (G ≃ₜ* G))`, and 'discrete group whose automorphism group is isomorphic to A' is `∃ (H : Type) (_ : Group H), Nonempty (MulAut H ≃* A)`.

In the `local_compactness_essential` slot I included the conjunct `¬ LocallyCompactSpace G`, making the claim strictly stronger than the bare negation of the LC-free implication: it asserts the counterexample is genuinely non-locally-compact, which is what 'the condition of local compactness is essential' is meant to show (and follows from the problem being posed as open after Wille's paper). A reviewer preferring the weaker reading could drop that conjunct.

The `cyclic` variant is stated positively and tagged `research solved` as the table requests, following the notebook's assertion 'This is true if A is cyclic'; no `formal_proof` attribute is attached since no formal proof exists.

The main slot quantifies over all locally compact G, including discrete/finite G where the claim is trivial (the included test theorem shows `MulAut G ≃* (G ≃ₜ* G)` for discrete G), as the notes anticipate.

reviewer_notes: All eight candidates compiled and were mutually consistent on the main and cyclic slots; the only substantive divergence was whether the essentiality slot includes `¬ LocallyCompactSpace G` (c05, c07 omit it; the other six include it). Both readings are true given Wille 1963; I shipped the stronger one, which pins the failure on non-local-compactness and is what the source remark means. Other modelling choices a reviewer should know: (1) topological automorphisms are bicontinuous (`Continuous f ∧ Continuous f.symm`); merely continuous automorphisms would be a different, weaker notion. (2) Hausdorffness (`T2Space G`) is a standing hypothesis in all three slots, per the notebook convention for locally compact groups; Mathlib's `LocallyCompactSpace` does not include it. (3) 'Discrete group' is an abstract group `H` with automorphism group `MulAut H` (justified by the shipped test `continuousMulAut_eq_top_of_discreteTopology`). (4) All carrier types live in `Type`, following the repo's Kourovka files; this is harmless for H (a group with finite automorphism group is countable) and is the standard idiom for the ∀ over G. (5) `Finite A` (not `Fintype`) and `Nonempty (_ ≃* _)` express finiteness and abstract isomorphism as propositions. The bespoke `continuousMulAut` is problem-local (kept in the problem file, not FormalConjecturesForMathlib) with an API lemma and a test. Final file compiles with only `declaration uses 'sorry'` warnings.
